questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">An organic compound A (C<sub>6<\/sub>H<sub>6<\/sub>O) gives dark green colouration with ferric chloride. On treatment with CHCl<sub>3<\/sub> and KOH, followed by acidification gives compound B. Compound B can also be obtained from compound C on reaction with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC). Identify A, B and C.** <\/strong><\/div>$\n$<div style=\"text-align:right\"> <\/div>$\n$
questions.explanation:
$ $ **Explanation:
$ To$ identify compounds A, B and C given: A (C$\u$2086H$\u$2086O) gives dark green with FeCl3 ; A → (CHCl3 / KOH, then acid) → B; B is also formed by oxidizing C with PCC.

$ $ **Concept:
$ This$ question is based on (1) Phenol test (FeCl3) (2) Reimer–Tiemann reaction (3) Oxidation of benzyl alcohol to aldehyde (PCC).
$ $
$ $**Solution:

$ $ A dark green or purple colour with FeCl3 indicates the presence of a phenol, as the phenolic –OH group forms a coloured complex with Fe3+ ions. Therefore, compound **A is phenol (C6H5OH).

$ $ When phenol is treated with CHCl3 and KOH (Reimer–Tiemann reaction), dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) is generated. This reacts with the phenoxide ion to introduce a –CHO group at the ortho position after hydrolysis. Thus, compound **B is o-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde).

$ $ PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) selectively oxidizes benzyl alcohols to benzaldehydes without further oxidation to acids. Hence, compound **C must be the corresponding benzyl alcohol.

$ $

$ $ **Final answer: (A)

$ $
$ $
